title: Decision: parent-dependent rooms take the subset reading, not room-policy-04's strict subset
description:
Needed before implementing bead mimid-1wgh.108. AGENTS.md requires a
decision bead citing the draft, the section, the competing readings, the
chosen reading and why.

THE TEXT. room-policy-04 §5 (txt L532-534): "In rooms with
parent_dependent set to true (a parent-dependent room), the list of
participants of the room MUST be a strict subset of the participants of
the parent room." And L530: "Only a single fixed-membership room can
exist for any unique set of participants."

Then L542-544, two paragraphs later: "Note: A room can be both
fixed_membership and parent_dependent, for example, for room used for a
multi-media call of clients in a Group DM."

THE CONTRADICTION. A call with everyone in the Group DM has the parent's
participant set, which is not a STRICT subset of it, so L533 forbids the
case L542 gives as its example. L530 forbids it a second way, since such
a call room would have the same participant set as the DM.

COMPETING READINGS:
(a) Strict, as written. The note's example is simply not constructible,
    and a call room must always omit at least one member of its parent.
(b) Subset. The note's example works, and the single-room rule does not
    count parent-dependent rooms.

CHOSEN: (b), subset.

WHY, and the first reason is the strongest:
- Reading (a) makes the specification's own example impossible. A
  reading under which the draft contradicts itself is weaker evidence of
  intent than one under which it does not.
- A call among everyone in a small room is the commonest call there is.
  Under (a), three people in a three-person DM cannot have a call room,
  which is absurd on its face.
- The keying analysis (bead mimid-96tt) concludes a call MUST have its
  own group, because mls-extensions §4.4's exported secret is computable
  by every member of the group it comes from. Under (a) a small room can
  never give a call its own group, so its calls cannot be confined at
  all. That is a security consequence of a wording choice, which argues
  it was not intended.
- We have asked. ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#40 raised it and PR #59
  proposes exactly this change. mimid implements what it asked for and
  will change if the WG says otherwise.

DEVIATION ACKNOWLEDGED. AGENTS.md says to implement the drafts as
written and to file a `wg` bead when the spec looks wrong. The `wg` part
is done (#40, #59). This is a deliberate departure from -04 as written,
and it is cheap to reverse: it is the difference between `is_subset` and
a strict-subset test in one place. The code cites this bead, and the
test suite carries a case documenting that reading (a) would forbid the
documented example, so the choice stays visible.

WHERE IT LANDS: mimid-server hub/update.rs already does cross-room
checks for the single-room rule (`fixed_rooms_elsewhere`), because
`RoomState` is per-room and the parent's participant list is not in it.
The parent check follows that pattern.
